title: Least tensor-supporting submodule for a flat Mittag-Leffler module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ a flat Mittag-Leffler $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-trf-mittag-leffler-module]. For every $R$-module $E$ and every $x\in E\otimes_R M$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], there exists a smallest submodule $E_0\subseteq E$ such that $x$ belongs to the image of $E_0\otimes_R M\to E\otimes_R M$ induced by inclusion; moreover this smallest submodule $E_0$ is a finite $R$-module.

proof.text: Let $i_N:N\hookrightarrow E$ denote inclusion and $T_N=i_N\otimes\mathrm{id}_M$. The submodules of $E$ form a set $\operatorname{Sub}_R(E)\subseteq\mathcal P(E)$. Define $\mathcal S=\{N\in\operatorname{Sub}_R(E):x\in\operatorname{im}T_N\}$. It contains $E$, because $i_E$ and its tensor map are identities [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Put $K=\bigcap_{N\in\mathcal S}N$ and $P=\prod_{N\in\mathcal S}E/N$. The intersection is a submodule by closure under addition and scalar multiplication; the map $q:E\to P$, $q(e)=(e+N)_{N\in\mathcal S}$, is linear componentwise.

source.place: Tag 0AS6 (lemma-minimal-contains), definition of the family I

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-ml-quotient-product-vanishing] to $J=\mathcal S$ and $N_j=j\subseteq E$. Its product and map are precisely $P$ and $q$: the $j$th component is $e+j$. For each fixed $j\in\mathcal S$, the support condition gives some $y\in j\otimes_R M$ with $T_j(y)=x$, exactly the image hypothesis; no compatible family of lifts is required. The given $M$ is Mittag-Leffler, so the lemma yields $(q\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(x)=0$.

Apply [lem-trf-flat-quotient-product-finite-lift] with the same set, family, $E$ and $x$: its intersection and map are $K$ and $q$. Flatness of $M$ and Step 2 meet its hypotheses. Obtain a finitely generated $L\subseteq K$ and $z\in L\otimes_R M$ mapping to $x$, so $L\in\mathcal S$. Let $a:L\hookrightarrow K$ be inclusion and put $y=(a\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(z)$. Since $i_Ka=i_L$, tensor compatibility with composition [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $(i_K\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(y)=x$. Thus $K\in\mathcal S$ as well.

source.place: Tag 0AS6 (lemma-minimal-contains), kernel and finite coefficient construction

proof.text: For any supporting submodule $N$, membership $N\in\mathcal S$ gives $K\subseteq N$. Since Step 3 gives $L\subseteq K$ and $L\in\mathcal S$, the inclusions $L\subseteq K\subseteq N$ show that $L$ itself is a least support. Taking $N=L$ gives $K\subseteq L$, so $K=L$. The finite list generating $L$ therefore generates $K$, and $E_0=K$ has both required properties. If $H$ is any other least support, its leastness gives $H\subseteq L$ and that of $L$ gives $L\subseteq H$, hence $H=L=K$. Thus smallest means least under inclusion, and finite means finitely generated over $R$.
